full_judgment:
Md. Nazrul Islam Talukder J: On an application under Section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure filed by the accused-petitioner, a Rule was issued calling upon the opposite-parties to show cause as to why the impugned proceedings of Joydevpur Police Station Case No. 11 of 2005 dated 11-12-2005 corresponding to GR No. 901 of 2005 under sections 341/379/506 (II) of the Penal Code, now pending before the Court of learned Magistrate, 1st Class, Gazipur should not be quashed and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 3. During investigation of the case, the police went to the place of occurrence, recorded the statements of the witnesses under Section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. Having found a prima-facie case, the police submitted charge-sheet No. 247 dated 8-5-2006 against the accused-petitioner alone under sections 341/323/379 7506(11) of the Penal Code. 

 4. At the time of the commencement of the trial, the accused-petitioner submitted an application under Section 241A of the Code of Criminal Procedure for discharging her from the case; but the learned Magistrate framed charge against the accused-petitioner under sections 341/379/506(11) of the Penal Code rejecting the application filed by the accused-petitioner. 

 6. At the very outset, Mr Hassan MS Azim, learned Advocate, appearing on behalf of the accused-petitioner, submits that the allegations brought against the accused-petitioner are totally false, fabricated, concocted, preposterous and self- contradictory, and that the same do not disclose any prima-facie case of theft and other offences against the accused-petitioner, and, as such, the initiation and continuation of the impugned proceedings are the abuse of the process of the Court, and in that view of the matter, the impugned proceedings should be quashed. He next submits that according to the allegations made in the FIR and the charge-sheet, the accused-petitioner and 7/8 unknown persons forcibly snatched away the mobile phones and some important papers from the informant and another and brought the covered van containing paper cartoons in front of a house at Segunbagicha; but it appears from order Nos. 7-5-2006, 22-3-2006 and 6-2-2006 that the customs authority seized all the alleged stolen goods which were brought out from the bonded ware house violating the order of injunction passed by the Company Court and violating the terms and conditions of the customs bond license, and, as such, the question of theft does not arise as per section 378 of the Penal Code, and in this perspective, the impugned proceedings being abuse of the process of the Court should be quashed. He then submits that from the admitted prosecution materials, the ingredients of offence of theft are not present, and, as such, the commission of offences under sections 341/506(11) of the Penal Code appears to be absurd and inconsistent, and from this stand point, the impugned proceedings are nothing but harassment to the accused-petitioner, and this being the position, the impugned proceedings being abuse of process of the Court should be quashed. He further submits that the alleged occurrence took place on 6-12-2005 at about 5-10 AM; but the informant lodged the ejahar with the Joydevpur police station on 11-12-2005, i.e. after 5 days, and, as such, the delay of 5 days in lodging the ejahar casts a flicker of doubt, and in that view of the matter, the impugned proceeding should be quashed. He categorically submits that the accused-petitioner was the former Managing Director of TaeHung Packaging (BD) Limited and that she was the former wife of Mr Bo Sun Park, the chairman of the said company; but the relationship between the husband and wife i.e. Chairman and the accused-petitioner became deteriorated over their family affairs and their relations became strained, and as a result, the Chairman of the TaeHung Packaging (BD) Limited took some unlawful steps for removing the petitioner from the post of Managing Director of the company and that the present case is the outcome of the grudge originated from the aforesaid personal dispute, and considering that aspect of the case, the impugned proceeding appears to be false and fabricated one and the same has been filed in order to cause harassment to the accused-petitioner. He candidly submits that the petitioner filed Company Matter No. 150/2005 before the Company Court and the Company Court by order dated 21-11-2005 passed an order of ad-interim injunction directing the Chairman of the TaeHung Packaging (BD) Limited from selling any movable and immovable properties of the company; but the Chairman of the company inspite of aforesaid injunction took steps for selling the goods of the company violating the Court's order and breaching the terms and conditions of the bond license, and as a result, the accused-petitioner informed the RAB forces of the aforesaid matter and the RAB under the leadership of a senior officer of RAB namely Major Maksudul Bari stopped the covered vans and arrested the said vans along with the goods which were, subsequently, brought before the custom office at segunbagicha and thereby the custom Authority seized all the goods and filed Custom Case No. 27 of 2005 on 12-12-2005; but the police of Joydevpur at the instance of the Chairman of the company filed this instant case against the accused-petitioner in order to cause harassment to the accused-petitioner adding different colour to the fact. He categorically submits that the police could not make any recovery of any goods from the possession of the accused-petitioner, and, as such„ it is crystal clear that the alleged occurrence was not happened in the way as has been alleged in the ejahar, and, as such, the impugned proceeding should be quashed. He lastly submits that the informant could not submit any medical certificate in support of the assault allegedly inflicted by the accused-petitioner upon the informant and another, and, as such„ the impugned proceeding should be quashed. 

 7. On the other hand, Mr M Amirul Islam learned Advocate along with Mr Md Taslim-uddin Bhuiyan, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of opposite-party No. 2, submits that the ejahar and the charge-sheet prima-facie disclose offences against the accused-petitioner under Sections 341/323/379/506(11) of the Penal Code, and in such a posture of things, the impugned proceedings should not be quashed. He next submits that the allegations brought against the accused-petitioner are all factual matters which may be resolved on taking evidence by the trial Court, and from this stand-point, the impugned proceedings should not be quashed. He lastly submits that whether the allegations brought against the accused-petitioner are true or false can only be decided on taking evidence by the trial Court, and that this Court sitting in its extra-ordinary jurisdiction cannot decide the factual aspect of the case invoking its jurisdiction under Section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure, and this being the scenario, the impugned proceeding should not be quashed. 

 8. We have gone through the application under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure and the materials annexed thereto. We have also considered the grounds taken in the miscellaneous case and the submissions advanced by the leaned Advocates for the respective parties. 

 9. In view of the submissions and counter-submissions advanced by the learned Advocate for the respective parties, an important question arises as to whether the impugned proceedings initiated against the accused-petitioner and others should be quashed. To decide this issue, it will be necessary to see the extent of the principles and categories of cases in which High Court Division may invoke its extra-ordinary power and authority under Section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure for quashing a proceeding. 

 10. In the case of Ali Akkas vs Enayet Hossain, 17 BLD (AD) 44 = 2 BLC (AD) 16, it has been spelt out that in order to bring a case within the purview of Section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure for the purpose of quashing a proceeding, one of the following conditions must be fulfilled: 

 (1) Interference even at an initial stage may be justified where the facts are so preposterous that even on admitted facts no case stands against the accused. 

 (4) In a case where the allegations in the FIR or the petition of complaint, even if taken at their face value and accepted in their entirety, do not constitute the offence as alleged. 

 (5) The allegations against the accused although constitute an offence alleged but there is either no legal evidence adduced in support of the case or the evidence adduced clearly or manifestly fails to prove the charge". 

 13. Under the circumstances, the husband of the petitioner took some unlawful steps for removing her from the post of Managing Director of the Company. Being aggrieved by the said steps, the accused-petitioner filed Company Matter No. 150 of 2005 before the Company Court. On 21-11-2005, the Company Court passed an order of injunction restraining the Chairman of the company from selling movable and immovable properties. However, the accused-petitioner came to know that in spite of the order of injunction, the Chairman of the company sent the paper cartoons i.e. the company's products to different companies on 6-12-2005 in the morning. Getting the aforesaid information, the accused-petitioner informed the RAB personnel and Customs Authority of the matter and accordingly, RAB personnel under the leadership of a senior officer Major Maksudul Bari stopped the covered van belonging to company and brought that covered van before the customs office. Accordingly, the customs authority seized all the alleged stolen goods for violation of the order of injunction and the terms and condition of the customs bond license and filed Customs Case No. 27 of 2005 dated 12-12-2005 against the Taehung packaging (BD) Ltd and the alleged stolen goods were kept in the godown of the customs authority. Anyway, it is alleged in the FIR that while the informant and another were carrying the goods in order to make delivery of the company's products to the different destinations, the accused-petitioner with the help of some persons intercepted the covered vans, took away the mobile phones along with other papers and snatched away the mobile phones and other necessary papers from the informant and another. The accused-petitioner and others took away mobile phones, cartoons and some necessary papers by committing theft and asked them to follow the car of the accused-petitioner as per their instruction. They also gave threat to kill them if they would not follow the instruction of the accused-petitioner and others. Subsequently, the accused-petitioner and others brought the covered van in front of a house at Sagunbagicha and told the drivers to leave the place and threatened to kill them. The informant and another thereafter left the place immediately being threatened by the accused-petitioner and accordingly, the informant filed the instant ejahar against the accused-petitioner and others under Sections 341/379/506(11) of the Penal Code. 

 14. It is a settled principle of law that the disputed questions of fact cannot be decided while exercising a jurisdiction under Section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure and that this is the function of the trial Court which would decide appropriately those facts on the basis of evidence to be adduced by the parties. If is also a settled principle of law that in a proceeding under Section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure, this Court should not be drawn in an inquiry as to the truth or otherwise of the facts which are not in the prosecution case. Besides, it is also well-settled that when the allegation brought against the accused-petitioner appears to be so preposterous and absurd that even on admitted facts no case stands against the accused-petitioner, in that case, this Court invoking its jurisdiction under Section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure can quash any proceeding. 

 15. Now, let us see as to whether the allegations brought against the accused-petitioner constitute offence of theft and other offences as has been alleged in the FIR. It is clearly stated in the FIR that accused-petitioner with the help of other accused snatched away two mobile phones, some cartoons and some necessary papers and brought the covered van in front of a house at Sagunbagicha and they also issued threat of killing. Beside the allegation made in the ejahar, we have gone through the order dated 7-5-2006 passed by the learned Magistrate, 1st Class, Gazipur in GR No. 901 of 2005, where from it appears that as per report submitted by one Md Tajul Islam, Assistant Commissioner, Customs Bond Commissionerate, 342/1, Segunbagicha, the custom authority seized two covered vans belonging to the Taehung Packing (BD) Ltd and filed one custom case against them. The said order dated 7-5-2006 runs as follows:- 

 18. In view of the aforesaid orders passed by the learned Magistrate, 1st Class, Gazipur, it is clear to us that the alleged stolen goods which were allegedly taken away or snatched away by the accused-petitioner were found to have been seized by the customs authority and those goods were found in the godown of the Custom Authority. Under the circumstances, it does not inspire our mind to believe that the alleged goods were taken away by the accused-petitioner with dishonest intention from the possession of the informant and another and the accused-petitioner committed the alleged offence of theft. Because the alleged goods were found to have been seized by the customs authority and found in the customs godown. The allegations against the accused-petitioner are that the accused-petitioner and others have committed theft by taking away Company's cartoons, two mobile sets and some necessary papers; but the fact remains that nothing was recovered from the possession of the accused-petitioner. Moreover, the alleged mobile sets of the informant and another, which were allegedly taken away by the accused-petitioner, were also found in the possession of the customs authority as stated in the seizure list. The records of the case do not indicate that the alleged seized mobile phones and other goods were recovered from the possession of the accused-petitioner. It may be noted here that the investigation officer submitted charge-sheet against accused-petitioner stating inter-alia that 

 But it is curious to note that none of the custom officials was examined under Section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure to know how and under what situation, the custom authority seized the alleged goods and filed the custom case against the Taehung packaging (BD) Limited. The police could have collected proper information on this matter from the custom authority; but they remained silent. The aforesaid fact has prompted us to believe that the alleged offences have not been committed in the manner stated in the ejahar and in the charge-sheet, and the police submitted a perfunctory police report against the accused-petitioner being influenced by the Chairman of Taehung packaging (BD) Limited. Under the circumstances, we do not find any ingredients of the offence of theft in the case, particularly when there is no prima-facie intention to remove any property from the possession of the inform-ant and another. 

 20. We have stated earlier that the ingredients of commission of theft against the accused-petitioner are not available in the prosecution materials. Since on the admitted facts no case of theft stands against accused-petitioner, the alleged offences as to wrongful restraint and criminal intimidation for the purpose of snatching the mobile phones and other goods from the informant and another appears to be absurd and preposterous. 

 21. It has been contended by the learned Advocate for opposite-party No. 2 that the allegations brought against the accused-petitioner prima-facie disclose offences against the accused-petitioner under Sections 341/379/506 of the penal Code and that those are disputed questions of fact which can be resolved on taking evidence by the trial Court. The learned Advocate for opposite-party No. 2, in support of his contentions, relied on the decision in the case of Md Shokrana vs State, 21 BLD (HCD) 296 = 5 BLC 611 and in the case of Jashim Uddin vs the State reported in 12 MLR (HCD) 93. On the other hand, the learned Advocate for the accused-petitioner has tried to impress our mind that it is true that the disputed questions of fact cannot be decided by this Court sitting in its extra-ordinary jurisdiction under Section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure but if the facts alleged in the FIR and other prosecution materials are found to be so preposterous and absurd that even on admitted facts, no case stands against the accused-petitioner, the initiation and continuation of the alleged proceedings against the accused-petitioner will be an engine of harassment, and in that case, this Court having jurisdiction under Section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure can quash the impugned proceedings. Learned Advocate for the accused-petitioner, in support of his contentions, relied on the case of Md Shokrana vs the state reported in 21 BLD (HCD) 296 = 5 BLC 611 wherein it has been held: 

 22. We have stated earlier that the accused-petitioner and her husband Mr Bo Sun Park are Korean citizens who came over Bangladesh in 1996 and invested a huge amount of money for the purpose of establishment of the company. However, by the passage of time, a dispute arises over their family affairs and company matters, and accordingly, the relationship between the accused-petitioner and her husband became very strained. Under the circumstances, her husband tried to remove the accused-petitioner from the post of Managing Director of the company. As a result, the accused-petitioner filed Company Matter No. 150 of 2005 before the High Court Division. The High Court Division by an order of injunction restrained Mr Bo Sun Park, the Chairman of the company from selling movable and immovable properties of the company; but the Chairman of the company violating the said order of injunction and breaching the terms and condition of the customs bond license tried to sell out the products of the company to different companies. Being informed of the same, the present accused-petitioner intimated this matter to the RAB personnel as well as customs authority. On getting information, the RAB personnel intercepted the covered vans along with the goods on the road, and deposited the same to the customs authority who ultimately seized the aforesaid materials and filed Customs Case No. 27 of 2005 on 12-12-2005 against the Taehung packaging (BD) Limited. In view of the above scenario, it appears that the accused-petitioner only gave information to the law enforcing agency and custom authority about the violation of the order of injunction passed by High Court Division and breaching of terms and conditions of the custom bond license. Now, question arises whether this act of the accused-petitioner constitutes an offence under sections 341/379/506(11) of the Penal Code. In order to come to a proper decision on this point, we have gone through sections 42, 43, 44 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. 

 23. Thus, the aforesaid provision of law imposes a legal duty upon every person aware of the commission of any offence or of the intention of any other person to commit any offence to give information thereof forthwith to the nearest Magistrate or Police-Officer. The purposes of this section have been designedly made so that crimes are brought to book and not suppressed by persons knowing about them. Moreover, refusal or omission to assist any public servant when bound by law to give assistance under this section is punishable offence under section 187 of the Penal Code. In the instant case, the accused-petitioner gave information to the RAB and the custom authority for commission of cognizable offences disclosing to the effect that the Chairman of the company namely Mr Bo Sun Park violating the order of injunction passed by the Company Court and breaching the terms and conditions of the customs bond license was sending the company's products to the different companies. By this act, the accused-petitioner has not committed any punishable offence; rather she has escaped herself from the commission of punishable offence by providing necessary information to the law enforcing agencies about the cognizable offences allegedly committed by the Chairman of the company. 

 24. From the foregoing discussions and regard being had to the facts and circumstances of the case and the propositions of law cited above, we are of the view that the impugned proceeding initiated against the accused-petitioner being preposterous and abuse of the process of the Court should not be allowed to continue and the same should be quashed for ends of justice. 

 25. Having considered all the aspects of the case, we find merit in this Rule. Accordingly, the Rule succeeds. 

 27. The impugned proceeding of Joydevpur Police Station Case No. 11 of 2005 dated 11-12-2005 corresponding to GR No. 901 of 2005 initiated against the accused-petitioner under sections 341/379/506(11) of the Penal Code, now pending in the Court of learned Magistrate, 1st Class, Gazipur is hereby quashed.
